# Executive summary

This project asks whether three structured MRI-derived measurements improve
subject-level dementia classification beyond a compact clinical feature set.
Five algorithms were compared under both feature settings using the same
persistent, entirely real held-out test set.

Balanced accuracy is the primary metric. With real-only training, the strongest
held-out values were **0.866** for clinical features and **0.839** for
clinical-imaging features. With 1:1 synthetic augmentation, the strongest
values were **0.902** and **0.933**, respectively. Every augmented point
estimate improved or tied its paired real-only estimate, but these exploratory
comparisons use the same 30 previously inspected test subjects and do not
establish that augmentation will generalize.

MMSE produced the largest held-out permutation-importance decrease in every
model/feature-set experiment. This describes model reliance in this sample; it
does not establish causality, clinical importance, or diagnostic validity.

# Data and study question

The [OASIS-2 longitudinal release](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2895005/)
contains MRI and associated clinical data from older adults with and without
dementia. The source paper reports 150 subjects and 373 imaging sessions. This
project uses the supplied longitudinal table and retains the complete row at
each subject's highest visit number.

```{python}
subject = data_assessment["subject_level"]
data_summary = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {"Stage": "Raw longitudinal", "Rows": data_assessment["raw"]["rows"],
         "Unique subjects": data_assessment["raw"]["unique_subjects"]},
        {"Stage": "Final-visit subject table", "Rows": subject["rows"],
         "Unique subjects": subject["unique_subjects"]},
        {"Stage": "Real training partition", "Rows": split_summary["train_subjects"],
         "Unique subjects": split_summary["train_subjects"]},
        {"Stage": "Real held-out partition", "Rows": split_summary["test_subjects"],
         "Unique subjects": split_summary["test_subjects"]},
    ]
)
show_table(data_summary, digits=0)
```

The binary target maps `Nondemented` to 0 and both `Demented` and `Converted`
to 1. Because predictors such as MMSE are measured contemporaneously with the
selected visit and outcome, this is a **classification** analysis—not early
detection, conversion forecasting, or prognosis.

## Feature settings

```{python}
feature_rows = []
for name, definition in model_config["feature_sets"].items():
    feature_rows.append(
        {
            "Feature setting": name,
            "Numeric predictors": ", ".join(definition["numeric"]),
            "Categorical predictors": ", ".join(definition["categorical"]),
        }
    )
show_table(pd.DataFrame(feature_rows))
```

Raw numeric `education_years` is retained. Identifiers, original diagnostic
group, visit metadata, handedness, and CDR are excluded from predictors. CDR is
treated as outcome-defining leakage.

# Leakage-safe experimental design

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["373 longitudinal visits"] --> B["Deterministic cleaning"]
  B --> C["150 final-visit subjects"]
  C --> D["120 real training subjects"]
  C --> E["30 real held-out subjects"]
  D --> F["Fold-local imputation, encoding, and scaling"]
  D --> S["Feature-set-specific, fold-local synthesis"]
  S --> F
  F --> G["Repeated stratified CV and tuning"]
  G --> H["Fixed final pipelines"]
  H --> I["One held-out evaluation"]
  E --> I
  I --> J["Bootstrap uncertainty and explanation"]
```

Subjects are split after deterministic cleaning and final-visit selection but
before learned preprocessing. Imputation, encoding, and scaling remain inside
scikit-learn pipelines and are learned separately within each training fold.
No subject appears in both partitions.

The 120-subject training partition contains 58 class-0 and 62 class-1
subjects. The held-out partition contains 14 class-0 and 16 class-1 subjects.
The same held-out subjects are used for every final experiment.

# Baselines and training-only model development

The baseline used repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation with 10
repeats. Hyperparameter selection used 15 shared training-only folds (five
folds repeated three times), with balanced accuracy as the selection metric.
Preprocessing was fitted inside each fold.

```{python}
baseline_table = baseline[
    ["algorithm", "feature_set", "balanced_accuracy_mean", "balanced_accuracy_std",
     "roc_auc_mean", "roc_auc_std"]
].rename(
    columns={
        "algorithm": "Algorithm",
        "feature_set": "Feature setting",
        "balanced_accuracy_mean": "Balanced accuracy mean",
        "balanced_accuracy_std": "Balanced accuracy SD",
        "roc_auc_mean": "ROC AUC mean",
        "roc_auc_std": "ROC AUC SD",
    }
)
show_table(baseline_table)
```

```{python}
tuning_table = tuning[
    ["algorithm", "feature_set", "balanced_accuracy_mean", "balanced_accuracy_std",
     "roc_auc_mean", "roc_auc_std"]
].rename(
    columns={
        "algorithm": "Algorithm",
        "feature_set": "Feature setting",
        "balanced_accuracy_mean": "Balanced accuracy mean",
        "balanced_accuracy_std": "Balanced accuracy SD",
        "roc_auc_mean": "ROC AUC mean",
        "roc_auc_std": "ROC AUC SD",
    }
)
show_table(tuning_table)
```

# Fixed held-out evaluation

The selected pipelines were fitted on all 120 real training subjects and then
evaluated on the persistent 30-subject real test partition. No threshold was
tuned; standard estimator predictions were used.

```{python}
held_out_table = test_metrics[
    ["algorithm", "feature_set", "balanced_accuracy", "roc_auc", "sensitivity",
     "specificity", "precision", "f1"]
].rename(
    columns={
        "algorithm": "Algorithm",
        "feature_set": "Feature setting",
        "balanced_accuracy": "Balanced accuracy",
        "roc_auc": "ROC AUC",
        "sensitivity": "Sensitivity",
        "specificity": "Specificity",
        "precision": "Precision",
        "f1": "F1",
    }
)
show_table(held_out_table)
```

![Balanced accuracy for the ten fixed held-out experiments.](../outputs/figures/test_balanced_accuracy.png){fig-alt="Grouped bar chart comparing balanced accuracy for five algorithms under clinical and clinical-imaging feature settings."}

![Held-out ROC curves.](../outputs/figures/test_roc_curves.png){fig-alt="ROC curves for the five algorithms in separate clinical and clinical-imaging panels."}

These estimates describe only this small held-out sample. They are not a basis
for clinical or deployment claims.

# Synthetic augmentation experiment

Phase 8 added one synthetic subject for every real training subject. Separate
Gaussian-copula generators were used for the two feature settings: the clinical
generator never received MRI-derived variables. During tuning, each generator
was fitted only on the real subjects in a fold's training subset; the fold's
validation subjects remained entirely real. Target-conditioned sampling
preserved the observed class counts rather than artificially balancing them.

For final training, each generator was fitted on the 120 real training subjects
and produced 120 unique synthetic subjects: 58 class 0 and 62 class 1. No
complete synthetic record exactly matched a real training record. The held-out
test set was never used for synthesis.

```{python}
quality_rows = []
for feature_set, values in synthetic_quality["reports"].items():
    quality_rows.append(
        {
            "Feature setting": feature_set,
            "Real rows": values["real_rows"],
            "Synthetic rows": values["synthetic_rows"],
            "Exact real matches": values["exact_real_matches"],
            "Diagnostic score": values["diagnostic_score"],
            "Quality score": values["quality_score"],
        }
    )
show_table(pd.DataFrame(quality_rows))
```

The SDV diagnostic checks structure and value validity. The quality score
summarizes marginal and pairwise statistical similarity; it is not a privacy
guarantee and does not guarantee predictive utility.

```{python}
augmented_table = synthetic_test_metrics[
    ["algorithm", "feature_set", "balanced_accuracy", "roc_auc", "sensitivity",
     "specificity", "precision", "f1"]
].rename(
    columns={
        "algorithm": "Algorithm", "feature_set": "Feature setting",
        "balanced_accuracy": "Balanced accuracy", "roc_auc": "ROC AUC",
        "sensitivity": "Sensitivity", "specificity": "Specificity",
        "precision": "Precision", "f1": "F1",
    }
)
show_table(augmented_table)
```

![Balanced accuracy across both training conditions.](../outputs/figures/training_condition_comparison.png){fig-alt="Grouped bar chart comparing held-out balanced accuracy across five algorithms, two feature sets, and real-only versus synthetically augmented training."}

```{python}
delta_table = condition_comparison.loc[
    condition_comparison["training_condition"] == "real_plus_synthetic",
    ["algorithm", "feature_set", "balanced_accuracy_delta_vs_real_only"],
].rename(
    columns={
        "algorithm": "Algorithm", "feature_set": "Feature setting",
        "balanced_accuracy_delta_vs_real_only": "Augmented - real-only",
    }
)
show_table(delta_table)
```

The largest point-estimate difference was +0.188 for the clinical-imaging
decision tree. These paired differences are descriptive. The augmentation
design and test set have not been evaluated in an independent cohort.

# Robustness and the MRI comparison

Stratified subject-level bootstrap resampling preserved the 14/16 class counts
in each of 5,000 replicates. Identical subject draws were used across models,
allowing paired clinical-imaging-minus-clinical comparisons.

```{python}
ba_intervals = intervals.loc[
    intervals["metric"] == "balanced_accuracy",
    ["algorithm", "feature_set", "estimate", "lower_bound", "upper_bound"],
].rename(
    columns={
        "algorithm": "Algorithm",
        "feature_set": "Feature setting",
        "estimate": "Estimate",
        "lower_bound": "95% lower",
        "upper_bound": "95% upper",
    }
)
show_table(ba_intervals)
```

![Balanced accuracy with percentile bootstrap intervals.](../outputs/figures/test_balanced_accuracy_intervals.png){fig-alt="Point estimates and broad 95 percent bootstrap intervals for all ten held-out experiments."}

```{python}
paired_table = paired_differences[
    ["algorithm", "estimate", "lower_bound", "upper_bound"]
].rename(
    columns={
        "algorithm": "Algorithm",
        "estimate": "Imaging - clinical",
        "lower_bound": "95% lower",
        "upper_bound": "95% upper",
    }
)
show_table(paired_table)
```

![Paired imaging-minus-clinical balanced-accuracy differences.](../outputs/figures/feature_set_balanced_accuracy_differences.png){fig-alt="Five paired feature-set differences whose intervals all cross or touch zero."}

Every paired interval includes zero. The available evidence therefore does not
show a stable held-out advantage from adding eTIV, nWBV, and ASF.

# Model explanations

Permutation importance provides one original-feature comparison across all 10
fixed models. It measures the held-out balanced-accuracy change after
permuting one feature; it does not refit a model or select features.

![Clinical permutation-importance matrix.](../outputs/figures/explain/permutation_importance_clinical.png){fig-alt="Feature-by-algorithm heatmap showing MMSE as the largest clinical permutation importance."}

![Clinical-imaging permutation-importance matrix.](../outputs/figures/explain/permutation_importance_clinical_imaging.png){fig-alt="Feature-by-algorithm heatmap showing MMSE as the largest clinical-imaging permutation importance."}

```{python}
top_permutation = (
    permutation.sort_values(
        ["algorithm", "feature_set", "importance_mean"],
        ascending=[True, True, False],
        kind="stable",
    )
    .groupby(["algorithm", "feature_set"], as_index=False, sort=True)
    .head(1)[["algorithm", "feature_set", "feature", "importance_mean", "importance_std"]]
    .rename(
        columns={
            "algorithm": "Algorithm",
            "feature_set": "Feature setting",
            "feature": "Top feature",
            "importance_mean": "Mean decrease",
            "importance_std": "SD",
        }
    )
)
show_table(top_permutation)
```

MMSE is the largest permutation feature in every experiment. Negative values
elsewhere mean permutation sometimes improved this small held-out score; they
are not evidence that a feature is protective or should be removed.

## Logistic coefficients

Numeric coefficients are expressed per one training-standard-deviation change.
The sex term is one male-versus-female contrast. Exponentiated coefficients are
adjusted model odds ratios, not causal effects.

![Logistic coefficient comparison.](../outputs/figures/explain/logistic_coefficients.png){fig-alt="Two panels showing signed standardized logistic coefficients for clinical and clinical-imaging models."}

```{python}
coefficient_table = coefficients[
    ["feature_set", "term", "coefficient", "odds_ratio", "unit"]
].rename(
    columns={
        "feature_set": "Feature setting",
        "term": "Term",
        "coefficient": "Coefficient",
        "odds_ratio": "Odds ratio",
        "unit": "Unit",
    }
)
show_table(coefficient_table)
```

## Tree SHAP

Tree SHAP [assigns additive feature contributions to individual model
predictions](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/hash/8a20a8621978632d76c43dfd28b67767-Abstract.html).
The decision-tree and random-forest explanations use class-1 probability units;
XGBoost uses raw-margin units. Magnitudes are not compared across these output
scales.

```{python}
top_shap = (
    shap_importance.sort_values(
        ["algorithm", "feature_set", "mean_absolute_shap"],
        ascending=[True, True, False],
        kind="stable",
    )
    .groupby(["algorithm", "feature_set"], as_index=False, sort=True)
    .head(3)
    .rename(
        columns={
            "algorithm": "Algorithm",
            "feature_set": "Feature setting",
            "feature": "Feature",
            "output_scale": "Output scale",
            "mean_absolute_shap": "Mean absolute SHAP",
        }
    )
)
show_table(top_shap[["Algorithm", "Feature setting", "Feature", "Output scale", "Mean absolute SHAP"]])
```

![XGBoost SHAP importance for clinical predictors.](../outputs/figures/explain/tree_shap/xgboost_clinical.png){fig-alt="Mean absolute raw-margin SHAP contributions for the clinical XGBoost model."}

![XGBoost SHAP importance with imaging predictors.](../outputs/figures/explain/tree_shap/xgboost_clinical_imaging.png){fig-alt="Mean absolute raw-margin SHAP contributions for the clinical-imaging XGBoost model."}

nWBV is prominent in the imaging tree-SHAP summaries but weak or negative
under permutation importance. This method-dependent pattern is compatible with
correlated predictors sharing information; it is not stable evidence that nWBV
has an independent or causal role.

# Limitations

- The held-out partition contains only 30 subjects, producing broad and
  sample-specific uncertainty.
- The highest-visit design is cross-sectional at the subject level and does
  not model trajectories or future conversion.
- MMSE is contemporaneous with the target and may dominate other predictors;
  the project does not claim screening performance without cognitive testing.
- Converted subjects are assigned to the dementia class by the confirmed
  project definition.
- Permutation importance can understate correlated variables.
- SHAP explains model behavior, not clinical importance, validity, or
  causality.
- No subgroup analysis, calibration study, externally validated threshold, or
  independent cohort evaluation was performed.
- Synthetic quality is based on only 120 real training subjects per generator;
  synthetic data may reproduce biases or reveal patterns from the source data
  and are not a privacy mechanism.

# Reproducibility

The canonical environment requires Python 3.12+, XGBoost 3.4.0, SHAP 0.52.0,
and SDV 1.37.3. The implementation uses scikit-learn pipelines
([Pedregosa et al., 2011](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v12/pedregosa11a.html)),
XGBoost ([Chen and Guestrin,
2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02754)), and SHAP ([Lundberg and Lee,
2017](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/hash/8a20a8621978632d76c43dfd28b67767-Abstract.html)).

Rendering this document reads the saved JSON, CSV, and PNG artifacts above. It
does not import project modeling modules, load fitted models, or rerun cleaning,
tuning, training, held-out evaluation, bootstrap validation, or explanation.

# Conclusion

This project demonstrates a reproducible, leakage-aware comparison of dementia
classification with and without structured MRI-derived variables and with and
without synthetic training augmentation. Augmentation improved or tied all ten
paired held-out point estimates, while the real-only bootstrap analysis did not
establish an MRI benefit. The small, reused test sample and absence of external
validation make these findings exploratory—not clinical evidence, a privacy
claim, or a diagnostic system.
